items.followUp: What is the least count of a vernier callipers with 10 vernier divisions equal to 9 main-scale divisions, if 1 main-scale division is 1 mm?

rubric.why: A vernier callipers is an instrument used to measure small lengths or dimensions accurately.
rubric.description: Identifies the instrument and its measuring purpose.
rubric.how: State that it is an instrument for accurately measuring small lengths or dimensions.

rubric.why: The least count is the difference between one main-scale division and one vernier-scale division; its usual value is 0.1 mm.
rubric.description: Gives the least-count relation or its usual value.
rubric.how: Write L.C. = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = 0.1 mm (0.01 cm).

modelAnswer: A vernier callipers is an instrument used to measure small lengths and dimensions, such as internal or external diameters, accurately.
Least count (L.C.) = 1 main-scale division − 1 vernier-scale division = 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm.

items.followUp: What are significant figures? State the number of significant figures in 0.00450 m.

rubric.why: Significant figures include the digits known with certainty and the first doubtful digit.
rubric.description: Identifies the certain digits and the first doubtful digit as significant.
rubric.how: State that significant figures include all digits known with certainty and the first doubtful digit.

modelAnswer: The significant figures of a measurement are all the digits known with certainty, together with the first doubtful or uncertain digit.

items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion and explain how it illustrates inertia.

rubric.why: The law says a body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion.
rubric.description: States the body's unchanged state of motion.
rubric.how: Mention that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform motion in a straight line.

rubric.why: An unbalanced external force is required to change the body's state of motion.
rubric.description: States the condition for changing the body's state.
rubric.how: Mention that the state changes only when an unbalanced external force acts.

modelAnswer: A body remains at rest, or continues to move with uniform velocity in a straight line, unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
This tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of motion is called inertia.

items.followUp: Write two differences between distance and displacement.

rubric.why: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on it.
rubric.description: Distinguishes mass and weight by their meanings.
rubric.how: State that mass measures the amount of matter and weight is the force of gravity on the body.

rubric.why: Mass is measured in kilograms and remains constant, while weight is measured in newtons and depends on gravitational acceleration.
rubric.description: Gives a further difference using units or dependence on gravity.
rubric.how: Compare their units, or state that mass remains constant while weight depends on gravitational acceleration.

modelAnswer: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, whereas weight is the gravitational force acting on the body.
Mass is measured in kilograms and remains constant; weight is measured in newtons and depends on the value of gravitational acceleration, g.
